# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 35 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 1 — The Two Angels

**1** "In the first commandment," he said, "I directed you to guard faith, fear, and self-control." "Yes, sir," I replied. **2** "Now," he said, "I want to show you the powers of these virtues so you may understand what each one is and how it operates. **3** Their powers are twofold, relating equally to the righteous and the unrighteous." **4** "How do you mean, sir?" "Listen," he said. "The righteous person possesses faith and fear and self-control. Now among the righteous there are two angels who dwell — one of righteousness and one of wickedness." **5** "But sir, how will I know their workings since both dwell within me?" **6** "Listen and understand," he replied. "The angel of righteousness is gentle, modest, peaceable, and sensitive. When this one enters your heart, immediately it speaks to you of righteousness, of purity, of holiness, of contentment, of every righteous deed, and of every glorious virtue. When all these things enter your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. **7** These are the works of the angel of righteousness. Trust him and trust his works. **8** Now consider also the works of the angel of wickedness. First of all, he is harsh, wrathful, and senseless, and his works are evil, pulling down the servants of God. Whenever this one enters your heart, recognize him by his works. **9** He generates in you anger, bitterness, and folly and every kind of wickedness. When these arise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is within you. Knowing his works, keep away from him and trust him in nothing."

---

*LOGOS note: The Two Angels teaching (Mandate 6) is the Shepherd's most explicit moral angelology. It parallels the Two Spirits of the Community Rule (1QS 3-4) and may represent Jewish-Christian teaching from common sources.*
